'''''Pimelea ferruginea''''', commonly known as '''pink rice flower'''<ref name="anpsa">{{cite web |title=''Pimelea ferruginea'' |url=https://anpsa.org.au/plant_profiles/pimelea-ferruginea/ |publisher=Australian Native Plants Society (Australia) |access-date=14 November 2022}}</ref> or '''coastal banjine''',<ref name="Rye1999">{{cite journal |last1=Rye |first1=Barbara L. |title=An updated revision of Pimelea sect. Heterolaena (Thymelaeaceae), including two new taxa. |journal=Nuytsia |date=1999 |volume=13 |issue=1 |pages=174–177 |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/225337#page/180/mode/1up |access-date=14 November 2022}}</ref> is a species of flowering plant in the family [[Thymelaeaceae]] and is [[endemic]] to near-coastal areas of [[Southwest Australia|south-western]] Western Australia. It is a dense, erect shrub with elliptic to narrowly elliptic leaves and head-like clusters of pale to deep pink, tube-shaped flowers.

==Description==
''Pimelea ferruginea'' is a dense, erect shrub that typically grows to a height of {{cvt|0.3–1.5|m}} and usually has a single stem at ground level. The leaves are elliptic to narrowly elliptic with the edges curved down, {{cvt|5–16|mm}} long and {{cvt|1.5–6.5|mm}} wide on a [[Petiole (botany)|petiole]] {{cvt|0.1–1|mm}} long. The flowers are pale to deep pink and borne in erect, head-like clusters on a hairy [[Peduncle (botany)|peduncle]] {{cvt|0.5–1.2|mm}} long, surrounded by 4 broadly egg-shaped [[bract]]s {{cvt|5–14|mm}} long, each flower on a hairy [[Pedicel (botany)|pedicel]] {{cvt|0.5–1.2|mm}} long. The [[Hypanthium|floral tube]] is {{cvt|7–13|mm}} long, the [[sepal]]s {{cvt|2.5–4|mm}} long. Flowering mainly occurs from August to February.<ref name="Rye1999" /><ref name="Rye">{{cite web |last1=Rye |first1=Barbara L. |title=''Pimelea ferruginea'' |url= https://profiles.ala.org.au/opus/foa/profile/Pimelea%20ferruginea |publisher=Flora of Australia. Australian Biological Resources Study, Department of Agriculture, Water and the Environment: Canberra |access-date=14 November 2022}}</ref><ref name="Rye1988">{{cite journal |last1=Rye |first1=Barbara L. |title=A revision of Western Australian Thymelaeaceae. |journal=Nuytsia |date=1988 |volume=6 |issue=2 |page=251 |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/232337#page/127/mode/1up |access-date=14 November 2022}}</ref>

==Taxonomy==
''Pimelea ferruginea'' was first formally described in 1805 by [[Jacques Labillardière]] in his ''[[Novae Hollandiae Plantarum Specimen]]''.<ref name=APNI>{{cite web|title=''Pimelea ferruginea''|url= https://id.biodiversity.org.au/instance/apni/476481 |publisher=APNI|access-date=14 November 2022}}</ref><ref name="Labill.">{{cite book |last1=Labillardière |first1=Jacques |title=Novae Hollandiae plantarum specimen |date=1805 |location=Paris |pages=10–11 |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/126969#page/9/mode/1up |access-date=14 November 2022}}</ref> The [[Binomial nomenclature|specific epithet]] (''ferruginea'') means "rust-coloured".<ref name="Sharr">{{cite book |last1=Sharr |first1=Francis Aubi |last2=George |first2=Alex |title=Western Australian Plant Names and Their Meanings |date=2019 |publisher=Four Gables Press |location=Kardinya, WA |isbn=9780958034180 |page=198 |edition=3rd}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
Pink rice flower grows on coastal sand dunes and rocky headlands in near-coastal areas between Cliff Head near [[Arrowsmith, Western Australia|Arrowsmith]], and [[Point Culver]], in the [[Esperance Plains]], [[Geraldton Sandplains]], [[Jarrah Forest]], [[Mallee bioregion|Mallee]], [[Swan Coastal Plain]] and [[Warren bioregion|Warren]] bioregions of south-western Western Australia.<ref name=FB>{{FloraBase|name=''Pimelea ferruginea''|id=5243}}</ref>

==Conservation status==
''Pimelea ferruginea'' is listed as "not threatened" by the Government of Western Australia [[Department of Biodiversity, Conservation and Attractions (Western Australia)|Department of Biodiversity, Conservation and Attractions]].<ref name="FB" />
